name: The Human Body and Medicine
description: How we learned how the body works and how to heal it: anatomy, blood, germs, vaccines and antibiotics, and the plagues and pandemics from Athens to COVID-19.

checkpoints.name: Ancient medicine and plagues
checkpoints.note: From skull surgery in the Stone Age to the healers of Egypt, India, Greece and China, and the first great plagues.

checkpoints.name: The Black Death and medieval medicine
checkpoints.note: Avicenna's Canon becomes the medical book of two worlds. The Black Death kills a third of Europe, and diseases from Europe devastate the Americas.

checkpoints.name: Anatomy and the microscope
checkpoints.note: Vesalius shows the body as it really is, Harvey shows that the heart pumps the blood round, and Leeuwenhoek sees cells and bacteria through his microscope.

checkpoints.name: Vaccines, germs and anaesthesia
checkpoints.note: Jenner's vaccine fights smallpox. Pasteur and Koch prove that germs cause disease, surgeons use anaesthetics and clean wounds, and X-rays show inside the body.

checkpoints.name: Antibiotics and insulin
checkpoints.note: Blood groups make transfusions safe, insulin treats diabetes and penicillin cures infections. The flu of 1918 kills tens of millions.

checkpoints.name: Transplants, scanners and HIV
checkpoints.note: The polio vaccine, the pill, the first heart transplant and CT and MRI scanners transform medicine. Smallpox is wiped out, and HIV spreads around the world.

checkpoints.name: Genes and new vaccines
checkpoints.note: The human genome is read and genes can be edited. COVID-19 brings the world to a halt, and new mRNA vaccines are made in less than a year.
